outcome: Not settled and no best-known exponent has moved since January 2024: the best unconditional exponent in every source I opened is still 13/84 (Bourgain, 2017), while in-window events are reformulations, a constant-only improvement, an analogue for another series or zeta-type function, a self-disclaimed heuristic, and unendorsed or withdrawn claimed proofs, with AI-involved results touching only zero counts and zero-free regions rather than the growth of zeta on the line.
problem_asks: One assertion about the Riemann zeta function on the critical line only: for every epsilon > 0, |zeta(1/2 + it)| = o(t^epsilon) as t tends to infinity. Parts: (1) the object is zeta on Re s = 1/2 (not off the line, not other L-functions, not zero counts); (2) the bound is required for every epsilon > 0 (the o-form and the O-form, |zeta(1/2+it)| = O(t^epsilon) for every epsilon > 0, are equivalent since epsilon is arbitrary); (3) the conclusion is that the growth exponent mu(1/2) equals 0 (Wikipedia's reformulation). Nothing else is asked: not the Riemann hypothesis, not zero density, not a rate.

events.what_happened: Bourgain, 'Decoupling, exponential sums and the Riemann zeta function', arXiv:1408.5794 (v1 25 Aug 2014; current v2 22 Feb 2016), later J. Amer. Math. Soc. 30 (2017) 205-224. A new decoupling inequality for curves gives a mean value theorem for exponential sums used in the Bombieri-Iwaniec method, improving the critical-line bound. EXPONENT CONFLICT: the arXiv abstract page (v1 and current, read through a summariser) quotes 53/342; the Wikipedia table lists both 53/342 and 13/84 as 'Bourgain 2017' and footnotes both to the JAMS paper; search snippets cite 13/84 as the JAMS exponent. The abstract says the terminal estimate conjectured by Lindelöf 'have been proved'; Theorem 1 as summarised: |zeta(1/2+it)| << t^epsilon for every epsilon > 0. Method: relations between bilinear forms of Hecke eigenvalues and Kloosterman sums. Math-Net lists it as Preprint 14 IAM, Khabarovsk, 1998.

This eventually was found to contain errors.' It gives no details of the errors and no source for the correction. A critique I first attributed to Ivić's arXiv math/0210337 does not mention Kuznetsov (that paper is about Hecke series moments; opened and checked). Motohashi-type criticism in search snippets concerns Kuznetsov's eighth-moment work, not this preprint, and I did not verify it.

events.what_happened: A. S. Fokas, 'A novel approach to the Lindelöf hypothesis', arXiv:1708.06607 (v1 10 Aug 2017; v5 12 Jun 2019; 55 pp.). Title history: v1 'A formal proof of a slight variant of Lindelöf's hypothesis'; v3 'A formal proof of Lindelöf's hypothesis'; v4-v5 'A novel approach to the Lindelöf hypothesis'. Derives a linear integral equation for |zeta(sigma+it)|^2 and analyses its large-t asymptotics for a related double exponential sum. The published version: 'A novel approach to the Lindelöf hypothesis', Transactions of Mathematics and Its Applications 3(1) (issue Feb 2019, article tnz006; online 13 Sep 2019). The journal text says the rigorous analysis covers two of four integrals and that 'The remaining results presented in this paper are formal'.

events.what_happened: J.-P. Kahane, 'The last problem of Harald Bohr', J. Austral. Math. Soc. (1989). Per the Furmaniak survey abstract (opened), Kahane answers Bohr's last problem in the form stated by constructing ordinary Dirichlet series whose derivative of the Lindelöf order function approaches -1/2, refuting the general version. Bohr had noted that a negative answer would imply the Lindelöf hypothesis for the alternating zeta series. The Kahane paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the general structure statement (Bohr's last problem); no bound on zeta(1/2+it).
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: A route to the hypothesis via Bohr's problem is closed in its general form; no direction on zeta itself.
events.object: Half-plane counterexamples and random constructions of ordinary Dirichlet series with derivative of the Lindelöf order approaching -1/2 (per Furmaniak's summary; not read directly).

Gives counterexamples to the Gonek-Graham-Lee conjecture that the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis holds for every admissible integer sequence; for generic real sequences the answer depends on the meaning of 'generic' (probability-one LH vs meagre LH sets); extends the RH-equivalence for primes to Beurling generalized number systems.

events.delivers: Counterexamples for a generalized (sequence) version of the hypothesis. Restriction: general sequences, not zeta.
events.remains: The classical hypothesis for zeta.

events.what_happened: André Unterberger, arXiv:2208.12937 (v1 27 Aug 2022, titled 'A pseudodifferential joint proof of the Riemann and Lindelöf hypotheses'; current v50 of 4 Sep 2026, titled 'Pseudodifferential arithmetic, Riemann and Lindelöf hypotheses'). The current abstract says that using Weyl symbolic calculus with a distribution built from the zeta zeros gives an operator whose estimates are equivalent to RH, and that 'A similar method leads to a proof of the Lindelöf hypothesis' (stated as unconditional). The v1 abstract says 'This leads to a proof of the conjecture'. The listing shows 50 versions.
events.revisions: 50 versions, v1 27 Aug 2022 to v50 4 Sep 2026. v18 (12 Jun 2024) retracts the RH proof: 'we claimed a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Not surprisingly, we just discovered an error in this attempt.' v40 (26 Dec 2025) claims a disproof of RH (zeros' real parts dense in [0,1]) and says the earlier argument was absurd. v48 (12 Aug 2026) marked withdrawn; v49 (20 Aug 2026) and v50 (4 Sep 2026) follow. v50 comment: 'A slight correction was needed at the end of the proof of Theorem 11.5'.
events.delivers: Claimed unconditional proof of the Lindelöf hypothesis by a method also claimed to give RH results. I did not locate the Lindelöf argument within the paper and did not read its body.
events.remains: None if the claim holds; I found no verification or critique.
events.doubts: (1) The author's own RH proof was retracted in v18 (June 2024) and an RH disproof was then claimed in v40 (Dec 2025); the Lindelöf claim was made in the same joint paper and is kept in v50. (2) A correction to Theorem 11.5 is recorded in the v50 comment; whether the Lindelöf argument uses that theorem is not established. (3) Versions v48 is withdrawn. (4) No referee report, journal acceptance, or expert critique found in any search.

events.what_happened: Lahoucine Elaissaoui, 'On the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Riemann Zeta function and Piltz divisor problem', arXiv:2406.00331 (v1 1 Jun 2024; v2 15 Apr 2025; 18 pp.). Derives the Fourier expansion of zeta^k(s) in Re s > 1/2 and a necessary and sufficient condition for the hypothesis, phrased via square-summable Fourier coefficients; gives a formula for the Piltz error term Delta_k(x) for almost all x. The search results list it as published in Mathematische Nachrichten (Wiley, doi 10.1002/mana.70081, online about Nov 2025 per a search snippet); the Wiley page returned HTTP 403, so the journal details are unverified.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jun 2024; v2 15 Apr 2025; Mathematische Nachrichten 2025 (per search snippet; not verified).
events.delivers: An equivalence: the hypothesis holds if and only if a condition on the Fourier expansion of zeta^k (square-summable coefficients) holds, per the abstract. Restriction: reformulation only; no bound on |zeta(1/2+it)| and no truth value established.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the equivalence does not decide the hypothesis.
events.doubts: The equivalence and its proof were not checked; the arXiv PDF body was unreadable through my tools; Wiley returned 403.
events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation of the hypothesis in a different form.

The abstract does not mention the Lindelöf hypothesis or mu(1/2). A search result links an Annals of Mathematics 2026 version (not opened).

events.what_happened: Terence Tao, Tim Trudgian, Andrew Yang, 'New exponent pairs, zero density estimates, and zero additive energy estimates: a systematic approach', arXiv:2501.16779 (v1 only, 28 Jan 2025). Reports four new exponent pairs, zero density estimates, and additive energy estimates, obtained by optimising relations among exponents in the Analytic Number Theory Exponent Database (ANTEDB). In the part I could read (first 100,000 of about 183,000 characters), the paper gives only the lower bound mu(sigma) >= max(0, 1/2 - sigma), says the hypothesis would make it sharp, defers all upper bounds for mu(1/2) to the ANTEDB, and gives mu(7/10) <= 3/40 as its one explicit mu bound.
events.revisions: v1 only (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: New exponent pairs and zero-density estimates; no new bound on mu(1/2) or on |zeta(1/2+it)| reported in the readable portion.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Partial read only; the ANTEDB listing, which the paper defers to for mu(1/2), was not opened.
events.direction: No movement of mu(1/2) reported in the part read.

events.what_happened: Ramūnas Garunkštis, Athanasios Sourmelidis, Jörn Steuding, 'The Lindelöf Hypothesis for Zeta Zero Ordinates', arXiv:2505.14228 (v1 only, 20 May 2025; 15 pp.). Gives conditional and unconditional asymptotic formulas for sums of gamma^(-i tau) over the imaginary parts gamma of the nontrivial zeros, and states: 'In particular, the obtained results are related to the Lindelöf Hypothesis for these ordinates' (in the sense of Gonek et al.). A DOI 10.1007/s11139-025-01208-1 is listed on the page, which suggests a journal version (not opened).

events.what_happened: Michael Revers, 'A new improved explicit estimate for zeta(1/2+it)', arXiv:2602.05614 (5 Feb 2026; 40 pp.). Theorem 1.1: |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.611 t^(1/6) log t for t >= 3, and <= 0.566 t^(1/6) log t for t >= 8.97*10^17. Improves the constant of Hiary-Patel-Yang via a refined explicit van der Corput method and computation. The paper says the exponent 1/6 'is also hard to improve'. Read through the first 100,000 of about 140,000 characters.
events.revisions: v1 5 Feb 2026 (later versions not checked).
events.delivers: Explicit constant improvement (0.611 and 0.566) with exponent 1/6 retained. Restriction: explicit constants only.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no change to the exponent.
events.doubts: The constants were read from Theorem 1.1 in the arXiv HTML; no second reader; the last 40,000 characters were not read.
events.direction: Constant-only improvement; does not move mu(1/2).

events.what_happened: Yuri Matiyasevich, 'An approach to the Lindelöf Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions', arXiv:2602.05731 (v1 5 Feb 2026; 21 pp.). Builds on the incomplete-gamma representation of Dirichlet L-functions; reports Taylor coefficients of the lower incomplete gamma function at infinity expressed via Touchard polynomials; uses them to reformulate the functional equation, which the author says 'explains' why |L(1/2+it)| should be small. Section 1 is a 'formula proof' of the hypothesis that the abstract itself disclaims: 'This is not a genuine proof, as we are not concerned with the convergence of our series nor do we justify changing the order of summation.' Section 2 proposes hypothetical routes to a rigorous proof.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: No rigorous result. A heuristic reformulation for Dirichlet L-functions (zeta as a special case) that the author disclaims as a proof.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: The author's own disclaimer (quoted above) states the argument is not a genuine proof.
events.direction: Heuristic in favour of smallness; the author does not claim a proof.

events.what_happened: Ralph Furmaniak, 'Bohr's Last Problem Under the Entirety Hypothesis: A Survey with Initial Reductions', arXiv:2603.23336 (24 Mar 2026; math.NT). Studies Bohr's last problem for Dirichlet series with entire continuation of order at most 1. Proposes an 'Analytic Lindelöf Hypothesis' (order function piecewise linear with integer slopes). Central object: the Cantor Dirichlet series L(s) = sum of nu-hat(n) n^(-s), nu the ternary Cantor measure. The abstract states 'we prove mu_L(1/2) <= 1/8 unconditionally' for this series, and that a Cantor-weighted Hurwitz second-moment conjecture would give mu_L(1/2) = 0. The title block of the arXiv HTML says: 'Portions of this work were developed in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic). The author is responsible for all errors.' The abstract page itself has no AI mention.
events.revisions: v1 24 Mar 2026 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Unconditional mu_L(1/2) <= 1/8 for the Cantor Dirichlet series (not zeta). Under a conjectural second-moment hypothesis, mu_L(1/2) = 0 for that series. Nothing unconditional about zeta(1/2+it).
events.remains: For zeta: all of problem_asks. For the Cantor series: mu_L(1/2) = 0 is conditional.
events.doubts: The bound concerns a different series, and the hypothesis for that series is an analogue of the Lindelöf hypothesis (the author's 'Analytic Lindelöf Hypothesis'). The 1/8 bound is claimed in the abstract only; the body was not read (the PDF returned compressed text; the HTML was read only in its title block and in part). The author says portions were developed with Claude but does not say which.
events.direction: An analogue of the exponent for a different series; cuts toward the hypothesis only by analogy and does not change zeta.
events.object: The ternary-Cantor-measure Dirichlet series L(s) = sum nu-hat(n) n^(-s), for which mu_L(1/2) <= 1/8 is claimed unconditionally (the Lindelöf order at sigma = 1/2 for that series).

events.what_happened: Takashi Miyagawa, 'Analogues of the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function and related problems', arXiv:2606.02407 (v1 1 Jun 2026; 8 pp.). Defines an analogue for the Barnes multiple zeta function zeta_r(s,a,(w_1..w_r)); establishes equivalent conditions for it in terms of integral mean values; the behaviour depends on the Q-rank of the w's. The abstract calls the Lindelöf hypothesis 'a major open problem' and says it is equivalent to certain mean-value estimates. A Pith automated review of this paper exists per search results (seen only in snippets; not opened).
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Equivalent mean-value conditions for an analogue (Barnes multiple zeta); no statement about the Riemann zeta function.
events.remains: All of problem_asks for zeta.

events.what_happened: Anthropic research post (dated 10 Aug 2026 in the post; arXiv:2608.13637, Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman, v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026, 21 pp.). An unreleased research version of Claude is reported to have raised the proven lower bound on the proportion of nontrivial zeros of zeta on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%. The arXiv claim: at least two-thirds of nontrivial zeros, counted with multiplicity, are simple and on the line, and at least five-sixths are distinct (constants 0.6725 and 0.8362 with a Montgomery-Taylor window). The post says RH is not proved and the technique is not expected to prove it. The result concerns zero proportions, not the size of zeta(1/2+it); the post and arXiv abstract do not mention the Lindelöf hypothesis.
events.revisions: Anthropic post 10 Aug 2026 (changelog update 13 Aug 2026); arXiv:2608.13637 v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: A zero-proportion result: at least 2/3 of nontrivial zeros (with multiplicity) simple and on Re s = 1/2; at least 5/6 distinct. Restriction: a statement about zeros, not about |zeta(1/2+it)| as t grows.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the growth of zeta(1/2+it) is not addressed.

events.what_happened: Youness Lamzouri, 'A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line', arXiv:2609.02882 (v1 2 Sep 2026; v2 8 Sep 2026; 17 pp.). Gives an unconditional proof that over 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the line and at least 83.62% are distinct, and two further estimates (88.76%, and an average of 83.62%) not in the Claude paper; replaces a finite-dimensional matrix framework with a Hilbert space inequality and uses Montgomery's pair correlation theorem. The abstract (summary read) says the Claude bounds were produced by an internal research version of Claude and verified by Alpöge and Furman.
events.revisions: v1 2 Sep 2026; v2 8 Sep 2026 (expanded exposition).
events.delivers: A second, human-written proof of a zero-proportion bound (67.25% simple and on the line; 83.62% distinct) plus two new estimates. Restriction: zero proportions only.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no statement about |zeta(1/2+it)|.
events.doubts: The AI attribution is from my reading of the abstract summary; I did not obtain the abstract's verbatim sentence, and the PDF body was unreadable.
events.direction: Not about the problem: zero proportions.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math repository (press reports the release on 6 or 7 Oct 2026; the README gives no date). The README says it 'contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model' and counts 719 manuscripts in 372 families (press says 722 manuscripts). Family 003 claims a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > 7/8 for every Dirichlet L-function, including zeta (the 'quasi-Riemann hypothesis'), per the catalogue and press; the README's human-edited writeup is for a zero-free region Re(s) > 11/12 for zeta. The Lean status is partial: 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations'; '~42% top-line results formalized'.
events.revisions: Repository; updates not tracked. Press dates 6 Oct and 7 Oct 2026 disagree.
events.delivers: Per the catalogue, a zero-free region Re(s) > 7/8 for all Dirichlet L-functions including zeta (or 11/12 in the README writeup; the sources disagree). Restriction: zero-free region near Re s = 1, not a bound on |zeta(1/2+it)|.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: a zero-free region to the right of the line does not bound zeta on the line.
events.doubts: The README says the manuscripts are not peer reviewed (press reports this; the README sentence I read does not say so explicitly). Family 003 and its Lean files were not opened. The 7/8 vs 11/12 figure conflicts between sources.
events.direction: Not about the problem: a zero-free region for zeta to the right of the line; no direction on |zeta(1/2+it)|.

disputes.summary: Bourgain's exponent: Wikipedia's table lists 53/342 and 13/84 both as 'Bourgain 2017' and cites the JAMS paper for both; the arXiv 1408.5794 abstract page, read through a summariser, gives 53/342 for v1 and the current version; search snippets give 13/84 for JAMS. I could not read the published abstract, so which exponent the paper states is unresolved.

Unterberger retracted an RH proof in v18 (June 2024), claimed an RH disproof in v40 (Dec 2025), kept an unconditional Lindelöf proof claim in v50 (Sep 2026), and marked v48 withdrawn (12 Aug 2026). The Lindelöf claim has not been checked by anyone I found.
The Exeter zeta page says Kuznetsov's 1998 preprint 'eventually was found to contain errors' without naming the errors or the source. I did not find the correction.

OpenAI's README counts 719 manuscripts in 372 families; press reports 722. The zero-free bound for Family 003 is 7/8 in the catalogue and press and 11/12 in the README's human-edited writeup. Press calls the 7/8 result the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, a name the README does not appear to use in the sentences I read.

Not a priority dispute, but a search summary attributed Shinya's arXiv 0706.0357 to the Lindelöf hypothesis and a Connes-Consani paper to 'Pseudodifferential arithmetic'; the arXiv pages show Shinya's paper concerns RH and that arXiv:2208.12937 is by Unterberger alone.

summary: Nothing in the window moves the best known exponent for zeta(1/2+it) or settles the hypothesis. Every source I opened gives the record as Bourgain's exponent (13/84 per JAMS 2017 and Wikipedia; the 2014 arXiv abstract as read says 53/342, unresolved). In-window items that touch the hypothesis by name are: Elaissaoui (arXiv 1 Jun 2024; Mathematische Nachrichten 2025 per a search snippet), an equivalence reformulation; Tao, Trudgian and Yang (Jan 2025), which report no new mu(1/2) bound in the part I could read; Garunkštis, Sourmelidis and Steuding (May 2025), a zero-ordinate variant; Revers (Feb 2026), which improves only the constant in the t^(1/6) log t bound (0.611, and 0.566 for very large t); Matiyasevich (Feb 2026), a heuristic the author says is not a proof; Furmaniak (Mar 2026), which claims mu_L(1/2) <= 1/8 for a Cantor Dirichlet series (not zeta) and says portions were developed with Claude (Anthropic); and Miyagawa (Jun 2026), an analogue for the Barnes zeta function. Older claimed proofs remain unendorsed preprints or withdrawn: Kuznetsov 1998 (the Exeter page says errors were found, unspecified), Aizenberg 2007 (withdrawn), Chaudhry 2010, Cheng-Wang-Albeverio 2010 (v8 withdrawn for disputed authorship), and Fokas 2017 (published 2019; the author's journal text says the remaining results are formal). Unterberger (2022) claims an unconditional proof and remains in v50 (Sep 2026) after reversals on RH and a withdrawn version. The AI-involved results touch zeros, not the growth of zeta on the line: Anthropic and Alpöge-Furman (10 to 13 Aug 2026) raised the proportion of zeros that are simple and on the line from 41.6% to 67.2%, and Lamzouri (Sep 2026) reproved a zero-proportion bound by a human route; OpenAI's openai/math repository (Oct 2026) claims a zero-free region Re(s) > 7/8 for all Dirichlet L-functions including zeta. In my reading none of these changes what the problem asks. The only AI attribution touching a Lindelöf-type quantity is Furmaniak's, which is about another series and does not say which portions Claude produced. Searches for AI-generated proofs of the hypothesis (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind Aletheia, AlphaEvolve, GPT-5, Gemini) found none specific to it. Close calls: (a) whether Furmaniak's mu_L(1/2) bound moves 'a quantity named in the problem' (I read it as an analogue, since mu_L is the Lindelöf order of a different series); (b) whether the zero-proportion and zero-free-region results bear on the hypothesis via Littlewood's zero-counting reformulation (I read them as not bearing, since they concern proportions of zeros on the line and regions to the right of it, not growth of zeta(1/2+it)); (c) whether the Unterberger claim should count while its RH claims were retracted and reversed (I record it as an unverified claim only).
competing_reading: One could treat the Anthropic-Alpöge-Furman zero results as bearing on the hypothesis because the hypothesis is equivalent to a zero-counting statement (Littlewood's N(sigma,T+1) - N(sigma,T) = o(log T) for sigma > 1/2), and a much stronger zero-proportion result is a step in that direction. I read the cited equivalence as concerning zeros near but right of the line, not the proportion on the line, so I do not count these as movement. Second, Furmaniak's mu_L(1/2) <= 1/8 could be read as moving an exponent with the same name for a Lindelöf-type order of a Dirichlet series, but the question names zeta(1/2+it) and the bound is for another series. Third, the Unterberger claim could be treated as the status-determining event if accepted; I found no check, and the author has retracted the RH claim made in the same paper.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The published abstract of Bourgain (JAMS 2017) to decide 13/84 vs 53/342. (2) Full text of Elaissaoui's Mathematische Nachrichten paper, to confirm the equivalence and its journal status. (3) A referee report or expert note on Unterberger's Lindelöf argument in v50, and the section containing it. (4) The Fokas companion publication, if any, and whether the 2019 journal version was refereed in a documented way. (5) Full text of Tao-Trudgian-Yang's mu(sigma) table and the ANTEDB entry for mu(1/2). (6) Revers's full text, to confirm no exponent change. (7) The openai/math Family 003 manuscript and Lean files, and whether any family addresses zeta on the critical line. (8) Furmaniak's full PDF, to see which portions were developed with Claude and whether the Cantor-series bound is used for zeta.
